sense: resume something from the point where it stopped
def: to start something again from the place where you stopped before
note: Muy común: pick up where we left off. Separable con objeto: pick it up tomorrow.
forms: pick up · picked up · picking up
errors_es: Decir 'continue where we stayed'. La fórmula natural es 'pick up where we left off'.

ex.en: Let's [pick up] where we left off yesterday.
ex.es: Sigamos donde nos quedamos ayer.

ex.en: After the commercial break, the host [picked up] the interview again.
ex.es: Después de los comerciales, el conductor retomó la entrevista.

ex.en: We'll [pick up] this conversation when you're calmer.
ex.es: Retomamos esta plática cuando estés más tranquilo.

sense: (of a vehicle) start moving away from a place or into traffic
def: to drive a car away from the side of the road, a driveway or a station
note: Pull out of the driveway / parking spot. Para trenes: the train pulled out of the station. Lo contrario: pull in.
forms: pull out · pulled out · pulling out
errors_es: Decir 'the car went out of the parking'. Natural: the car pulled out of the parking spot.

ex.en: Check your mirror before you [pull out] into traffic.
ex.es: Revisa el espejo antes de incorporarte al tráfico.

ex.en: The bus was [pulling out] just as we got there.
ex.es: El camión iba saliendo justo cuando llegamos.

ex.en: A truck [pulled out] of the driveway without looking.
ex.es: Una camioneta salió de la cochera sin fijarse.

sense: go out somewhere for a short time
def: to leave a place quickly for a short time and then come back
note: Informal. Suele ir con for/to: pop out for coffee. También: algo que sale de repente (his eyes popped out).
forms: pop out · popped out · popping out
errors_es: Usar 'go out a moment' de forma rígida. 'I'm just popping out' suena mucho más natural.

ex.en: I'm just [popping out] to grab some milk.
ex.es: Nada más salgo un momento por leche.

ex.en: She [popped out] for lunch, but she'll be right back.
ex.es: Salió un momento a comer, pero ya regresa.

ex.en: Can you watch my bag while I [pop out]?
ex.es: ¿Me cuidas la mochila mientras salgo un momento?

sense: write something down so you don't forget it
def: to write something short, like a number or idea, so you remember it
note: Separable: note it down. Más hablado: write it down o jot it down.
forms: note down · noted down · noting down
errors_es: Decir 'take note of the number' cuando solo se escribe. 'Note it down' es apuntarlo.

ex.en: Let me [note down] your phone number real quick.
ex.es: Déjame anotar tu número rápido.

ex.en: I [noted down] everything the doctor said.
ex.es: Apunté todo lo que dijo el doctor.

ex.en: Please [note down] any questions for the end of the meeting.
ex.es: Por favor anoten sus preguntas para el final de la junta.

sense: open a door, usually as an order ("Police, open up!")
def: to open a door so someone can come in, often said loudly while knocking
note: Típico de series policiacas: Police! Open up! También para un negocio que abre por la mañana.
forms: open up · opened up · opening up
errors_es: Decir 'open the door!' siempre. En una orden urgente, 'Open up!' es lo natural.

ex.en: Police! [Open up] or we're coming in!
ex.es: ¡Policía! ¡Abran o vamos a entrar!

ex.en: I banged on the door, but nobody [opened up].
ex.es: Toqué fuerte la puerta, pero nadie abrió.

ex.en: Come on, [open up], it's freezing out here!
ex.es: ¡Ándale, ábreme, que hace un frío horrible aquí afuera!

sense: keep moving and not stay in one place (often a police order)
def: to go forward and not stop or stand in one place
note: Clásico de policía: Move along, folks, nothing to see here. También: things are moving along = avanzar bien.
forms: move along · moved along · moving along
confuse: move on (superar; pasar a otra cosa)
errors_es: Decir 'circulate' como en español. 'Circulate' en inglés es para aire, documentos o rumores.

ex.en: [Move along], folks, there's nothing to see here.
ex.es: Circulen, señores, aquí no hay nada que ver.

ex.en: The guard told us to [move along] and stop blocking the exit.
ex.es: El guardia nos dijo que siguiéramos avanzando y no tapáramos la salida.

ex.en: Traffic is finally [moving along] after the accident.
ex.es: Por fin el tráfico está avanzando después del choque.

sense: take the exact amount of something you need
def: to take a certain amount of something, like flour or medicine, using a cup or spoon
note: Separable: measure it out. Común en recetas e instrucciones de medicinas.
forms: measure out · measured out · measuring out
errors_es: Decir solo 'measure two cups'. Se entiende, pero 'measure out two cups' es la forma natural en recetas.

ex.en: [Measure out] two cups of flour before you start.
ex.es: Mide dos tazas de harina antes de empezar.

ex.en: The nurse carefully [measured out] the medicine for the baby.
ex.es: La enfermera midió con cuidado la medicina para el bebé.

ex.en: I always [measure out] my coffee so it's not too strong.
ex.es: Siempre mido el café para que no quede muy cargado.

sense: clean up spilled liquid with a mop or cloth
def: to remove liquid from a floor or table using a cloth or a mop
note: Separable: mop it up. En noticias también: terminar de resolver lo que queda (mop up after a storm).
forms: mop up · mopped up · mopping up · mop-up (sustantivo)
errors_es: Confundir 'mop' con 'trapo'. 'Mop' es el trapeador; 'mop up' es secar o limpiar lo derramado.

ex.en: Grab a towel and [mop up] that juice before someone slips.
ex.es: Agarra una toalla y seca ese jugo antes de que alguien se resbale.

ex.en: We spent all night [mopping up] after the pipe burst.
ex.es: Pasamos toda la noche secando el agua después de que se reventó el tubo.

ex.en: The waiter [mopped up] the spilled wine in seconds.
ex.es: El mesero limpió el vino derramado en segundos.

sense: remove a thin layer, sticker or tight piece of clothing
def: to take off something thin that is stuck to a surface, or to take off wet or tight clothes
note: Separable: peel it off. Intransitivo: the paint is peeling off = se está despegando. También un carro que se separa del grupo.
forms: peel off · peeled off · peeling off
errors_es: Usar 'take off the sticker' siempre. Para algo pegado, 'peel off' es lo natural.

ex.en: Can you help me [peel off] this price tag?
ex.es: ¿Me ayudas a despegar esta etiqueta del precio?

ex.en: She [peeled off] her wet jacket and sat by the fire.
ex.es: Se quitó la chamarra mojada y se sentó junto al fuego.

ex.en: The paint is [peeling off] the walls in the basement.
ex.es: La pintura se está despegando de las paredes del sótano.

sense: play a recording again to watch or hear it
def: to play sound or video that was recorded, so you can hear or see it again
note: Separable: play it back. Sustantivo: playback (velocidad de reproducción). En series policiacas: play back the security footage.
forms: play back · played back · playing back · playback (sustantivo)
errors_es: Decir 'reproduce the video'. 'Reproduce' en inglés es reproducirse (biología) o copiar.

ex.en: Can you [play back] that last part of the video?
ex.es: ¿Puedes volver a poner la última parte del video?

ex.en: The detective [played back] the security footage three times.
ex.es: El detective reprodujo el video de seguridad tres veces.

ex.en: When I [played back] my voice message, I sounded so nervous.
ex.es: Cuando escuché mi mensaje de voz, me oí bien nervioso.

sense: do a test, class or work hours you missed earlier
es: reponer; recuperar (un examen, una clase, horas)
def: to do work, a test or a class later because you missed it the first time
note: Separable: make it up. Sustantivo: a make-up test/exam (examen de reposición). Muy común en escuelas de EE. UU. y Canadá.
forms: make up · made up · making up · make-up exam
errors_es: Decir 'recover the exam'. En inglés no se 'recupera' un examen: se 'makes it up'.

ex.en: I was sick on Monday, so I have to [make up] the quiz.
ex.es: Estuve enfermo el lunes, así que tengo que reponer el examen.

ex.en: She [made up] the lost hours by working Saturday.
ex.es: Repuso las horas perdidas trabajando el sábado.

ex.en: Can I [make up] the lab next week?
ex.es: ¿Puedo reponer la práctica la próxima semana?

sense: get into a car or small space quickly, all together
def: to get into a vehicle or room quickly as a big group
note: Inseparable: pile into the car. Lo contrario: pile out of. Da idea de grupo y algo de desorden.
forms: pile into · piled into · piling into
errors_es: Decir 'we all entered the car'. 'Enter' suena formal; 'we piled into the car' es lo natural.

ex.en: We all [piled into] Jake's car and headed to the lake.
ex.es: Nos metimos todos en el carro de Jake y nos fuimos al lago.

ex.en: The kids [pile into] the kitchen as soon as dinner's ready.
ex.es: Los niños se meten en bola a la cocina en cuanto está la cena.

ex.en: Six of us [piled into] a tiny elevator.
ex.es: Nos metimos seis apretujados en un elevador diminuto.

sense: record the time you start work on a time clock
def: to record the time you arrive at work, using a card or a machine
note: EE. UU. y Canadá. Salida: punch out. Sinónimo: clock in. También 'punch in a code' = teclear un código.
forms: punch in · punched in · punching in
errors_es: Decir 'check in' para el trabajo. 'Check in' es en hotel o aeropuerto; en el trabajo es punch in o clock in.

ex.en: Don't forget to [punch in] as soon as you get here.
ex.es: No se te olvide checar en cuanto llegues.

ex.en: He [punched in] five minutes late again.
ex.es: Volvió a checar cinco minutos tarde.

ex.en: I'm [punching in] at six tomorrow, so I can't stay out.
ex.es: Mañana entro a las seis, así que no puedo desvelarme.

sense: change someone's look or a place so it looks completely new
def: to change how a person, room or thing looks so it seems new and better
note: Separable: make it over. El sustantivo makeover (cambio de look) es mucho más frecuente que el verbo.
forms: make over · made over · making over · makeover (sustantivo)
errors_es: Decir 'make a change of look'. Natural: get a makeover / give the kitchen a makeover.

ex.en: They [made over] the old garage into a home office.
ex.es: Convirtieron la cochera vieja en una oficina en casa.

ex.en: The show [makes over] one tiny apartment every week.
ex.es: El programa transforma un departamento chiquito cada semana.

ex.en: We're [making over] the guest room before my parents visit.
ex.es: Estamos renovando el cuarto de visitas antes de que vengan mis papás.

sense: use all the money or capacity available, especially on a credit card
es: topar; llegar al límite (de la tarjeta)
def: to use the full amount of credit or space you have, so there is nothing left
note: Separable: max it out. Intransitivo: the server maxed out = llegó a su límite. Muy común: maxed out my credit card.
forms: max out · maxed out · maxing out
errors_es: Decir 'I finished my card'. Lo natural es 'I maxed out my card'.

ex.en: I [maxed out] my credit card on the trip.
ex.es: Topé mi tarjeta de crédito en el viaje.

ex.en: If you keep [maxing out] your cards, your score will drop.
ex.es: Si sigues topando tus tarjetas, va a bajar tu historial.

ex.en: The new storage [maxes out] at two terabytes.
ex.es: El almacenamiento nuevo llega a un máximo de dos terabytes.

sense: become calmer and more relaxed
def: to become less nervous, angry or stressed and more easygoing
note: Muy coloquial, tono relajado. 'Mellow out, man' = cálmate. También con la edad: he's mellowed out = se ha vuelto más tranquilo.
forms: mellow out · mellowed out · mellowing out
errors_es: Traducirlo como 'madurar' de fruta. Aquí es calmarse o volverse más tranquilo.

ex.en: Hey, [mellow out], it's just a game.
ex.es: Oye, cálmate, nada más es un juego.

ex.en: My dad has really [mellowed out] since he retired.
ex.es: Mi papá se ha vuelto mucho más tranquilo desde que se jubiló.

ex.en: I need a weekend at the cabin to [mellow out].
ex.es: Necesito un fin de semana en la cabaña para relajarme.

sense: raise the price of something to make a profit
def: to make the price of something higher than what it cost, to earn money
note: Separable: mark it up. Sustantivo: markup (margen de ganancia). También: corregir un texto con anotaciones.
forms: mark up · marked up · marking up · markup (sustantivo)
errors_es: Decir 'they raised up the price'. Para tiendas y márgenes: mark up.

ex.en: Airports always [mark up] snacks like crazy.
ex.es: En los aeropuertos siempre le suben un montón a la botana.

ex.en: The store [marked up] the jackets right before winter.
ex.es: La tienda subió el precio de las chamarras justo antes del invierno.

ex.en: Restaurants usually [mark up] wine by two or three times.
ex.es: Los restaurantes suelen cobrar el vino al doble o al triple.

sense: get a better job or a higher position
def: to get a more important job or a higher level in a company or ranking
note: Común: move up in the company / move up the ladder. En entrevistas: I want to move up into management.
forms: move up · moved up · moving up
errors_es: Decir 'ascend in the company'. 'Ascend' suena muy formal; lo natural es move up.

ex.en: She [moved up] to manager in less than two years.
ex.es: Subió a gerente en menos de dos años.

ex.en: I'd like to [move up] into a leadership role here.
ex.es: Me gustaría subir a un puesto de liderazgo aquí.

ex.en: Our team [moved up] three spots in the rankings.
ex.es: Nuestro equipo subió tres lugares en la tabla.

sense: say or feel that you disagree with or dislike something
def: to say that you do not agree with or do not like something
note: Después de 'to' va sustantivo o -ing: I object to working weekends. En juicios: Objection, Your Honor!
forms: object to · objected to · objecting to · objection (sustantivo)
errors_es: Decir 'I object to work' en vez de 'to working'. Aquí 'to' es preposición y pide -ing.

ex.en: I [object to] being treated like a child.
ex.es: No acepto que me traten como a un niño.

ex.en: The neighbors [objected to] the new parking lot.
ex.es: Los vecinos se opusieron al nuevo estacionamiento.

ex.en: Does anyone [object to] moving the meeting to Friday?
ex.es: ¿Alguien tiene problema con mover la junta al viernes?

sense: (an idea) come into someone's mind
es: ocurrírsele a; pasarle por la mente
def: if an idea comes to you, you suddenly think of it
note: La idea es el sujeto: It never occurred to me (that)... Muy común en discusiones: Did it ever occur to you to call?
forms: occur to · occurred to · occurring to
errors_es: Decir 'I occurred an idea'. El sujeto es la idea: an idea occurred to me / it occurred to me.

ex.en: Did it ever [occur to] you to just call me?
ex.es: ¿Nunca se te ocurrió simplemente llamarme?

ex.en: It never [occurred to] me that she was lying.
ex.es: Nunca se me pasó por la mente que estuviera mintiendo.

ex.en: Has it [occurred to] anyone that the door was unlocked?
ex.es: ¿A alguien se le ha ocurrido que la puerta estaba sin llave?

sense: keep telling someone what to do in a bossy way
def: to give someone orders all the time, as if you were their boss
note: Siempre separado: order someone around. Muy común en peleas: Stop ordering me around!
forms: order around · ordered around · ordering around
errors_es: Decir 'stop ordering me'. Sin 'around' suena incompleto; lo natural es 'stop ordering me around'.

ex.en: Stop [ordering me around], you're not my dad!
ex.es: ¡Deja de mandonearme, no eres mi papá!

ex.en: Her new boss [orders everyone around] all day.
ex.es: Su nuevo jefe se la pasa dando órdenes a todo el mundo.

ex.en: I'm tired of being [ordered around] by my older brother.
ex.es: Ya me cansé de que mi hermano mayor me esté mandoneando.

sense: perform surgery on a person or part of the body
def: to cut open someone's body to fix or remove something, as a surgeon does
note: En inglés se dice operate ON someone, no operate someone. Pasiva: he was operated on yesterday. Típico de series médicas.
forms: operate on · operated on · operating on
errors_es: Decir 'they operated my mom' o 'I was operated'. Falta 'on': they operated on my mom / I was operated on.

ex.en: They need to [operate on] her knee right away.
ex.es: La tienen que operar de la rodilla de inmediato.

ex.en: The surgeon who [operated on] my dad was amazing.
ex.es: El cirujano que operó a mi papá fue increíble.

ex.en: We can't [operate on] him until his fever goes down.
ex.es: No lo podemos operar hasta que le baje la fiebre.

sense: look so similar that people believe you are someone or something else
es: pasar por; parecer (algo que no es)
def: to be accepted as someone or something because you look or seem like them
note: Sin intención de engañar (a diferencia de pass off as). Común: she could pass for twenty. Sarcasmo: what passes for dinner here.
forms: pass for · passed for · passing for
confuse: pass off as (hacer pasar por, con engaño)
errors_es: Usar 'pass as' y 'pass for' como si 'for' fuera 'para'. Aquí significa 'parecer' o 'dar el gatazo'.

ex.en: With that beard, you could [pass for] a lumberjack.
ex.es: Con esa barba podrías pasar por leñador.

ex.en: She's forty but easily [passes for] thirty.
ex.es: Tiene cuarenta, pero fácil pasa por de treinta.

ex.en: This fake ID wouldn't [pass for] real anywhere.
ex.es: Esta identificación falsa no pasaría por real en ningún lado.

sense: end an argument and become friendly again
def: to fix a relationship after a fight so people are on good terms again
note: Frase fija: patch things up (with someone). Separable: patch it up. También: curar de forma rápida una herida.
forms: patch up · patched up · patching up
errors_es: Decir 'fix the relation'. Natural: patch things up with someone.

ex.en: Have you two [patched things up] yet?
ex.es: ¿Ya se arreglaron ustedes dos?

ex.en: He called his sister to [patch up] their fight.
ex.es: Le llamó a su hermana para arreglar su pleito.

ex.en: They're trying to [patch up] their marriage for the kids.
ex.es: Están tratando de arreglar su matrimonio por los niños.

sense: pay a large amount of money, e.g. a prize, claim or settlement
def: to give a big sum of money, usually from an insurance company, a bet or a court decision
note: Sustantivo: payout. Intransitivo: the policy didn't pay out = el seguro no pagó.
forms: pay out · paid out · paying out · payout (sustantivo)
errors_es: Confundir con 'pay off'. Pay out = el dinero sale hacia otro (premio, seguro); pay off = terminar de pagar.

ex.en: The insurance company finally [paid out] for the flood damage.
ex.es: La aseguradora por fin pagó por los daños de la inundación.

ex.en: That slot machine hasn't [paid out] all night.
ex.es: Esa máquina no ha soltado nada en toda la noche.

ex.en: The city will [pay out] millions to settle the lawsuit.
ex.es: La ciudad va a pagar millones para cerrar la demanda.

sense: reduce a debt by making payments
def: to make the amount you owe smaller by paying part of it
note: Muy de EE. UU. y Canadá: pay down your mortgage / credit card. A diferencia de pay off, no implica terminar de pagar.
forms: pay down · paid down · paying down
errors_es: Decir 'pay off' cuando solo se reduce la deuda. Pay down = bajarla; pay off = liquidarla.

ex.en: We're using my bonus to [pay down] the credit card.
ex.es: Vamos a usar mi bono para bajarle a la tarjeta.

ex.en: She [paid down] half her student loans in three years.
ex.es: Pagó la mitad de su crédito estudiantil en tres años.

ex.en: It's smart to [pay down] high-interest debt first.
ex.es: Conviene ir bajando primero la deuda con intereses altos.

sense: eat only small amounts of food, without interest
def: to eat very little of your food, slowly, because you are not hungry or are upset
note: Inseparable: pick at your food. Señal de tristeza o enfermedad en series. También: rascarse (una costra, un hilo).
forms: pick at · picked at · picking at
errors_es: Usar 'eat little by little'. Para comer sin ganas, lo natural es 'pick at your food'.

ex.en: You're just [picking at] your salad. Are you okay?
ex.es: Nada más estás picoteando tu ensalada. ¿Estás bien?

ex.en: He [picked at] his dinner and went to bed early.
ex.es: Apenas probó la cena y se fue a dormir temprano.

ex.en: Stop [picking at] that scab or it'll get infected.
ex.es: Deja de rascarte esa costra o se te va a infectar.

sense: (of the police) arrest or take someone to the station
def: if the police take someone, they stop them and bring them to the station
note: Separable: pick him up. Muy de series policiacas: We picked him up two blocks away. Más neutro que arrest.
forms: pick up · picked up · picking up
errors_es: Pensar que siempre es 'pasar por alguien'. Con la policía como sujeto significa detener.

ex.en: The cops [picked him up] outside the bar last night.
ex.es: La policía lo detuvo afuera del bar anoche.

ex.en: Get a warrant and [pick up] the suspect.
ex.es: Consigue una orden y detén al sospechoso.

ex.en: She was [picked up] for shoplifting when she was sixteen.
ex.es: La detuvieron por robar en una tienda cuando tenía dieciséis.

sense: start talking to a stranger to begin a romantic or sexual encounter
def: to meet someone you don't know, often at a bar, and try to start a romantic relationship
note: Separable: pick her/him up. Pickup line = frase para ligar. Tono informal; puede sonar despectivo.
forms: pick up · picked up · picking up · pickup line
errors_es: Usar 'flirt' cuando hay intención de llevarse a alguien. 'Flirt' es coquetear; 'pick up' es ligar.

ex.en: Did that guy just try to [pick you up]?
ex.es: ¿Ese tipo te acaba de querer ligar?

ex.en: He thinks he can [pick up] anyone with that cheesy line.
ex.es: Cree que puede ligarse a quien sea con esa frase cursi.

ex.en: They met when she [picked him up] at a wedding.
ex.es: Se conocieron cuando ella lo ligó en una boda.

sense: become more cheerful or energetic, or make someone feel that way
def: to start to feel happier or more awake, or to make someone feel this way
note: Intransitivo: she perked up when she heard the news. Transitivo: coffee perks me up. También sube la economía o las ventas.
forms: perk up · perked up · perking up
errors_es: Decir 'animate' para personas. 'Animate' es dar vida (dibujos animados); para personas: perk up o cheer up.

ex.en: A strong coffee always [perks me up] in the morning.
ex.es: Un café cargado siempre me reanima en la mañana.

ex.en: The dog [perked up] as soon as he heard the leash.
ex.es: El perro se animó en cuanto oyó la correa.

ex.en: She was quiet all day, but [perked up] at dinner.
ex.es: Estuvo callada todo el día, pero se animó en la cena.

sense: emphasize something to make it seem more important or attractive
es: resaltar; exagerar (lo bueno o lo dramático)
def: to make something seem bigger or more important than it is, or to call attention to it
note: Lo contrario de play down. Separable: play it up. En entrevistas: play up your strengths.
forms: play up · played up · playing up
errors_es: Decir 'exaggerate' cuando solo es resaltar algo positivo. Play up puede ser simplemente destacar.

ex.en: [Play up] your sales experience in the interview.
ex.es: En la entrevista resalta tu experiencia en ventas.

ex.en: The news really [played up] the drama between the two families.
ex.es: Las noticias exageraron mucho el drama entre las dos familias.

ex.en: He's [playing up] his injury to get out of practice.
ex.es: Está exagerando su lesión para no ir al entrenamiento.

sense: finish food or a task quickly and completely
def: to eat or drink all of something quickly, or to finish a job fast
note: Separable: polish it off. Da idea de rapidez y gusto: he polished off the whole pizza.
forms: polish off · polished off · polishing off
errors_es: Traducirlo como 'pulir'. Con comida significa acabársela por completo.

ex.en: The kids [polished off] the whole pizza in ten minutes.
ex.es: Los niños se acabaron toda la pizza en diez minutos.

ex.en: Want to [polish off] this last bit of ice cream?
ex.es: ¿Te quieres acabar este poquito de helado que queda?

ex.en: I'll [polish off] this report and then we can go.
ex.es: Termino este reporte y ya nos vamos.

sense: improve a skill or a piece of work by practicing or editing it
def: to make a skill or a piece of work better by practicing or changing small things
note: Separable: polish it up. Común con résumé, presentation, English, French. Casi sinónimo de brush up on.
forms: polish up · polished up · polishing up
errors_es: Decir 'improve up'. El verbo es polish (dar brillo) + up.

ex.en: I need to [polish up] my résumé before I apply.
ex.es: Tengo que pulir mi currículum antes de postularme.

ex.en: She's [polishing up] her French for the move to Montreal.
ex.es: Está puliendo su francés para la mudanza a Montreal.

ex.en: Let's [polish up] the slides before the client meeting.
ex.es: Hay que pulir las diapositivas antes de la junta con el cliente.

sense: look around a place, often in things that aren't yours
def: to search or look through a place casually, sometimes where you shouldn't
note: Con in o en lugar: poke around in my stuff / poke around the attic. En series: don't go poking around in my business.
forms: poke around · poked around · poking around
errors_es: Decir 'search around' cuando hay curiosidad indiscreta. Poke around tiene ese matiz de husmear.

ex.en: Why were you [poking around] in my closet?
ex.es: ¿Por qué andabas husmeando en mi clóset?

ex.en: I [poked around] the antique shop for an hour.
ex.es: Estuve curioseando una hora en la tienda de antigüedades.

ex.en: Stop [poking around] in things that aren't your business.
ex.es: Deja de meterte en lo que no te importa.

sense: arrive in large numbers or amounts
def: to come in great numbers, like messages, money, people or offers
note: Muy de noticias: donations are pouring in. Con personas: fans poured into the stadium (pour into).
forms: pour in · poured in · pouring in
errors_es: Usar 'arrive a lot'. Para mensajes o donativos que no paran, lo natural es 'pour in'.

ex.en: Messages have been [pouring in] since the video went viral.
ex.es: Han estado lloviendo mensajes desde que el video se hizo viral.

ex.en: After the fire, donations [poured in] from all over Canada.
ex.es: Después del incendio, llegaron donativos de todo Canadá.

ex.en: Complaints are [pouring in] about the new update.
ex.es: Están llegando quejas a montones por la nueva actualización.

sense: move in front of others in a race, competition or market
def: to get in front of a competitor, in a race, a game or business
note: Con of: pull ahead of the other team. Común en deportes, carreras y ventas.
forms: pull ahead · pulled ahead · pulling ahead
errors_es: Decir 'go in front of'. En competencias: pull ahead (of).

ex.en: The Oilers [pulled ahead] in the third period.
ex.es: Los Oilers tomaron la delantera en el tercer periodo.

ex.en: Our product is finally [pulling ahead] of the competition.
ex.es: Nuestro producto por fin le está ganando a la competencia.

ex.en: She [pulled ahead] in the last lap and won.
ex.es: Se adelantó en la última vuelta y ganó.

sense: separate people or animals that are fighting
def: to separate two people or animals that are fighting
note: Separable: pull them apart. También: desarmar algo en piezas, o criticar duramente (como pick apart).
forms: pull apart · pulled apart · pulling apart
errors_es: Decir 'separate them' sin más en una pelea. Se entiende, pero 'pull them apart' es lo natural.

ex.en: It took three guys to [pull them apart].
ex.es: Se necesitaron tres tipos para separarlos.

ex.en: The teacher [pulled apart] the two boys in the hallway.
ex.es: La maestra separó a los dos niños en el pasillo.

ex.en: I had to [pull the dogs apart] before someone got bitten.
ex.es: Tuve que separar a los perros antes de que mordieran a alguien.

sense: attract people or earn money in large amounts
def: to get a lot of people to come, or to earn a lot of money
note: Separable: pull them in. Común: pull in crowds / customers / $2 million. También: llegar un tren o carro y detenerse.
forms: pull in · pulled in · pulling in
errors_es: Usar 'attract' siempre. Para multitudes y ganancias, pull in suena más natural en conversación.

ex.en: The food trucks [pull in] huge crowds every summer.
ex.es: Los food trucks atraen muchísima gente cada verano.

ex.en: Her bakery [pulls in] about ten grand a month.
ex.es: Su panadería saca como diez mil al mes.

ex.en: We need a promo that [pulls in] younger customers.
ex.es: Necesitamos una promoción que atraiga clientes más jóvenes.

sense: (of the police) make a driver stop at the side of the road
es: parar; marcarle el alto (la policía a un conductor)
def: if the police stop your car, they make you drive to the side of the road
note: Separable y casi siempre con pronombre en medio: a cop pulled me over. Pasiva: I got pulled over.
forms: pull over · pulled over · pulling over · get pulled over
errors_es: Decir 'the police stopped my car' está bien, pero 'I got pulled over' es lo más común al contarlo.

ex.en: I got [pulled over] for a broken taillight.
ex.es: Me paró la policía por una calavera rota.

ex.en: The officer [pulled him over] for speeding near the school.
ex.es: El oficial lo paró por exceso de velocidad cerca de la escuela.

ex.en: Why do they always [pull me over] on this road?
ex.es: ¿Por qué siempre me paran en esta carretera?

sense: kill a sick, old or dangerous animal painlessly
def: to kill an animal with drugs, usually because it is very sick or old
note: Separable: put him down. Eufemismo frecuente; más suave: put to sleep. Tema delicado en dramas familiares.
forms: put down · put down · putting down
errors_es: Decir 'sacrifice the dog'. 'Sacrifice' suena a ritual; lo natural es put down o put to sleep.

ex.en: We had to [put our old dog down] last spring.
ex.es: Tuvimos que dormir a nuestro perro viejito la primavera pasada.

ex.en: The vet said it was kinder to [put him down].
ex.es: El veterinario dijo que era más humano sacrificarlo.

ex.en: They won't [put down] a healthy horse.
ex.es: No van a sacrificar a un caballo sano.

sense: add someone's name to a list or write something on a form
es: apuntar; anotar (en una lista o formulario)
def: to write a name or answer on a list or form
note: Muy hablado: Put me down for two tickets. En formularios: What should I put down for my address?
forms: put down · put down · putting down
errors_es: Decir 'write me in the list'. Natural: put me down (for something) / put my name down.

ex.en: Sure, [put me down] for the potluck.
ex.es: Claro, apúntame para la comida de traje.

ex.en: What should I [put down] as my emergency contact?
ex.es: ¿A quién pongo como contacto de emergencia?

ex.en: I [put my name down] for the hockey league.
ex.es: Me apunté a la liga de hockey.

sense: pretend to have a feeling, accent or way of behaving
es: fingir; poner (un acento, una cara, una actitud)
def: to pretend to feel or be something that you are not
note: Común: put on an accent / a brave face / an act. 'It's all an act, she's putting it on' = está fingiendo.
forms: put on · put on · putting on
errors_es: Decir 'make a fake accent'. Natural: put on an accent; para disimular: put on a brave face.

ex.en: He [puts on] a British accent when he's nervous.
ex.es: Pone acento británico cuando está nervioso.

ex.en: She [put on] a brave face at the funeral.
ex.es: Se hizo la fuerte en el funeral.

ex.en: I don't think he's sick, he's [putting it on].
ex.es: No creo que esté enfermo, está fingiendo.

sense: organize or present an event, show or meal
def: to organize a show, party, class or meal for other people
note: Común: put on a play / a show / a fundraiser / a spread (comida). Separable: put it on.
forms: put on · put on · putting on
confuse: put on (poner música o la tele)
errors_es: Decir 'make a show'. Para organizar un espectáculo o evento: put on a show.

ex.en: The school is [putting on] a musical in December.
ex.es: La escuela va a montar un musical en diciembre.

ex.en: They [put on] an amazing barbecue for the whole street.
ex.es: Organizaron una carne asada increíble para toda la calle.

ex.en: We're [putting on] a fundraiser for the food bank.
ex.es: Estamos organizando un evento para recaudar fondos para el banco de alimentos.

sense: stop letting a problem or disagreement affect you, for now
def: to ignore a feeling or disagreement for a while so you can do something important
note: Frase muy común: put aside our differences. Separable: put it aside.
forms: put aside · put aside · putting aside
errors_es: Decir 'leave aside the differences' es correcto pero menos natural que 'put aside our differences'.

ex.en: Let's [put aside] our differences and finish this project.
ex.es: Dejemos de lado nuestras diferencias y terminemos este proyecto.

ex.en: She [put aside] her pride and called him first.
ex.es: Se tragó el orgullo y le llamó ella primero.

ex.en: For one night, can we [put aside] the drama?
ex.es: ¿Por una noche podemos dejar de lado el drama?

sense: fare or do in a situation ("How did you make out?")
es: irle a uno (bien o mal); salir de algo
def: to have a certain result in a situation, good or bad
note: Informal, EE. UU. y Canadá: How did you make out at the interview? = ¿Cómo te fue? Ojo al contexto para no confundir con besarse.
forms: make out · made out · making out
errors_es: Entenderlo siempre como 'besarse'. Con 'how' y una situación significa '¿cómo te fue?'.

ex.en: So how did you [make out] at the job interview?
ex.es: ¿Y cómo te fue en la entrevista de trabajo?

ex.en: We [made out] pretty well at the garage sale.
ex.es: Nos fue bastante bien en la venta de cochera.

ex.en: How are you [making out] with the new puppy?
ex.es: ¿Cómo te va con el cachorro nuevo?

sense: get revenge on someone for something bad they did
def: to do something bad to someone because they did something bad to you
note: Casi siempre separado: I'll pay you back for this. Sustantivo: payback (venganza) — Payback's a... (frase de series).
forms: pay back · paid back · paying back · payback (sustantivo)
errors_es: Pensar que solo es devolver dinero. En amenazas ('I'll pay you back for this') es vengarse.

ex.en: Don't worry, I'll [pay him back] for what he did.
ex.es: No te preocupes, me voy a desquitar por lo que hizo.

ex.en: She [paid her ex back] by telling everyone his secret.
ex.es: Se vengó de su ex contándole a todos su secreto.

ex.en: He's been planning to [pay them back] for months.
ex.es: Lleva meses planeando cómo vengarse de ellos.

sense: arrange a meeting or date that may change later
def: to plan a meeting or event for a time, knowing it might still change
note: Separable: pencil me in for Tuesday. Como escribir con lápiz: se puede borrar.
forms: pencil in · penciled in · penciling in (Canadá: pencilled)
errors_es: Decir 'schedule provisionally' de forma rígida. 'Can I pencil you in for Friday?' es lo natural.

ex.en: Can I [pencil you in] for Thursday at ten?
ex.es: ¿Te puedo apartar el jueves a las diez, tentativamente?

ex.en: We've [penciled in] the launch for early March.
ex.es: Tenemos el lanzamiento agendado tentativamente para principios de marzo.

ex.en: I'll [pencil in] lunch with your team, but no promises.
ex.es: Aparto la comida con tu equipo, pero no te prometo nada.

sense: claim or suggest that something is true, often falsely
def: to say or suggest something is true when it may not be
note: Estructuras: make out that... / make someone out to be... (He made me out to be a liar). Suele ir con queja.
forms: make out · made out · making out · make someone out to be
errors_es: No reconocer 'make me out to be' = pintarme como. 'She made me out to be the bad guy' = me pintó como el malo.

ex.en: He [made out] that he'd never met her before.
ex.es: Hizo creer que nunca la había visto antes.

ex.en: She [made me out] to be the bad guy in front of everyone.
ex.es: Me pintó como el malo frente a todos.

ex.en: It's not as bad as the news is [making out].
ex.es: No está tan mal como lo pintan las noticias.

sense: help to cause a particular result or experience
es: hacer que sea; dar como resultado
def: to cause or help create a certain situation or quality
note: Muy natural: That makes for a great story / an awkward dinner. Otro sentido: dirigirse a (make for the exit).
forms: make for · made for · making for
errors_es: Decir 'make a good story' cuando quieres decir que algo produce una buena historia: 'That makes for a good story'.

ex.en: Rain and no heat [made for] a miserable camping trip.
ex.es: La lluvia y la falta de calefacción hicieron del campamento un horror.

ex.en: Clear goals [make for] much shorter meetings.
ex.es: Las metas claras hacen que las juntas sean mucho más cortas.

ex.en: Well, that's going to [make for] an awkward Thanksgiving.
ex.es: Bueno, eso va a hacer que el Día de Acción de Gracias sea incómodo.

sense: have a casual or secret sexual relationship, often while with someone else
es: andar con alguien; tener un amorío
def: to have a romantic or sexual relationship that is not serious, often secretly
note: Con with: mess around with someone. On: mess around on someone = ponerle el cuerno. Muy de series.
forms: mess around · messed around · messing around
errors_es: Entenderlo siempre como 'hacer relajo'. Con 'with someone' o 'on someone' habla de amoríos o infidelidad.

ex.en: Everyone knew he was [messing around] with his assistant.
ex.es: Todos sabían que andaba con su asistente.

ex.en: Are you [messing around] on me?
ex.es: ¿Me estás poniendo el cuerno?

ex.en: They [messed around] a few times in college, nothing serious.
ex.es: Anduvieron un par de veces en la universidad, nada serio.

sense: affect someone badly, emotionally or physically
def: to harm someone's mind or feelings, or to hurt their body badly
note: Separable: it messed him up. Adjetivo: messed up (traumado; también 'qué mal' = that's messed up).
forms: mess up · messed up · messing up · messed up (adjetivo)
errors_es: Pensar que solo es 'regarla'. 'The divorce really messed him up' = el divorcio lo dejó muy mal.

ex.en: Losing his dad that young really [messed him up].
ex.es: Perder a su papá tan joven lo dejó muy mal.

ex.en: That movie [messed me up] for days.
ex.es: Esa película me dejó traumado varios días.

ex.en: The crash [messed up] his back pretty badly.
ex.es: El choque le dejó la espalda bastante mal.

sense: get someone involved in something bad or illegal (usually passive)
def: to make someone part of a bad or dangerous situation
note: Casi siempre: get/be mixed up in something / with someone. Don't get mixed up with those guys.
forms: mix up · mixed up · mixing up · get mixed up in
errors_es: Entenderlo como 'confundirse'. 'He got mixed up in drugs' = se metió en drogas.

ex.en: How did a nice kid get [mixed up] in all this?
ex.es: ¿Cómo se metió un buen muchacho en todo esto?

ex.en: Don't [mix me up] in your family drama.
ex.es: No me metas en tu drama familiar.

ex.en: She got [mixed up] with the wrong crowd in high school.
ex.es: Se juntó con malas compañías en la prepa.

sense: speak rudely or angrily, especially to someone in authority
def: to talk in a rude, loud or disrespectful way, often to a parent, teacher or boss
note: Con to: mouth off to the teacher. Típico de padres regañando: Don't you mouth off to me!
forms: mouth off · mouthed off · mouthing off
errors_es: Decir 'answer badly'. Para un hijo respondón: talk back o mouth off.

ex.en: Don't you dare [mouth off] to me, young man.
ex.es: Ni se te ocurra contestarme feo, jovencito.

ex.en: He got suspended for [mouthing off] to the principal.
ex.es: Lo suspendieron por ponerse respondón con el director.

ex.en: She always [mouths off] when she's had a few drinks.
ex.es: Siempre se pone a decir de cosas cuando ya se tomó unas copas.

sense: come closer to someone in order to attack, catch or take control
def: to get close to a person or place to catch, attack or take it over
note: Inseparable. Policías y criminales: police moved in on the house. También en amor o negocios: quitarle algo a otro.
forms: move in on · moved in on · moving in on
errors_es: Confundirlo con 'move in' (mudarse). Con 'on' significa cercar o ir por algo o alguien.

ex.en: SWAT [moved in on] the warehouse just before dawn.
ex.es: El equipo táctico cercó la bodega justo antes del amanecer.

ex.en: A bigger company is [moving in on] our market.
ex.es: Una empresa más grande se está metiendo a nuestro mercado.

ex.en: He [moved in on] my girlfriend while I was away.
ex.es: Le tiró la onda a mi novia mientras yo no estaba.

sense: manage to do something without the right skills, plan or resources
def: to succeed in doing something even though you are not organized or don't know how
note: Intransitivo: we'll muddle through. Transitivo: muddle through the first week. Tono modesto o autocrítico.
forms: muddle through · muddled through · muddling through
errors_es: Decir 'survive it'. Para algo hecho sin saber bien cómo: muddle through.

ex.en: I don't speak much French, but I [muddled through] in Quebec.
ex.es: No hablo mucho francés, pero me las arreglé en Quebec.

ex.en: We'll [muddle through] somehow until the new manager starts.
ex.es: De alguna forma saldremos del paso hasta que llegue el nuevo gerente.

ex.en: She [muddled through] her first week without any training.
ex.es: Sacó como pudo su primera semana sin ninguna capacitación.

sense: move around slowly feeling sad and doing nothing
es: andar de capa caída; andar deprimido
def: to spend time feeling sorry for yourself without trying to feel better
note: Muy de amigos o familia: Stop moping around and call her. También mope around the house.
forms: mope around · moped around · moping around
errors_es: Decir 'be sad around'. Para quien se arrastra triste por la casa: mope around.

ex.en: Stop [moping around] and go out with us tonight.
ex.es: Ya deja de andar de capa caída y sal con nosotros hoy.

ex.en: He's been [moping around] the house since the breakup.
ex.es: Ha andado deprimido por la casa desde que cortaron.

ex.en: I [moped around] all weekend after I didn't get the job.
ex.es: Anduve de bajón todo el fin de semana después de que no me dieron el trabajo.

sense: (a doubt or worry) keep bothering you
es: no dejar en paz; traer inquieto (una duda)
def: if a thought or worry stays in your mind and bothers you for a long time
note: Sujeto típico: something, a feeling, a thought. Something's been nagging at me = algo me trae inquieto. Con personas, nag = dar lata.
forms: nag at · nagged at · nagging at · nagging (adjetivo: a nagging feeling)
errors_es: Pensar que solo es 'regañar'. Con una idea como sujeto significa que no te deja en paz.

ex.en: Something about his story keeps [nagging at] me.
ex.es: Algo de su historia no me deja en paz.

ex.en: The doubt [nagged at] her for weeks.
ex.es: La duda la tuvo inquieta durante semanas.

ex.en: What's been [nagging at] you all day?
ex.es: ¿Qué es lo que te ha traído inquieto todo el día?

sense: fit a lot of activities or people into a limited time or space
es: meter mucho (en poco tiempo o espacio)
def: to manage to do or include many things in a short time or small space
note: Separable: pack a lot in. También: atraer público (the show packs them in). 'Pack it in' = dejarlo ya (más británico).
forms: pack in · packed in · packing in
errors_es: Decir 'we did many things in little time' es correcto, pero 'we packed a lot in' es más natural.

ex.en: We [packed in] four museums in one day.
ex.es: Nos metimos a cuatro museos en un solo día.

ex.en: They [packed in] so many seats that nobody could move.
ex.es: Metieron tantas sillas que nadie se podía mover.

ex.en: You [packed a lot in] for a three-day trip.
ex.es: Hiciste un montón para ser un viaje de tres días.

sense: get rid of something unwanted by making someone else take it
def: to trick or push someone into accepting something you don't want, like a bad job or object
note: Estructura: palm something off on someone. Separable: palm it off on me. También: palm someone off with an excuse.
forms: palm off · palmed off · palming off
errors_es: Decir 'give me the bad thing'. Para endilgarle algo a otro: palm it off on someone.

ex.en: He always [palms off] the boring tasks on the interns.
ex.es: Siempre les endilga las tareas aburridas a los becarios.

ex.en: They tried to [palm off] a broken TV on us.
ex.es: Nos quisieron encajar una tele descompuesta.

ex.en: Don't let her [palm you off] with another excuse.
ex.es: No dejes que te salga con otra excusa.

sense: give someone money to keep quiet or do something dishonest
def: to give someone money so they stay quiet or help you do something wrong
note: Separable: pay him off. Sustantivo: payoff (soborno). Típico de dramas policiacos y judiciales.
forms: pay off · paid off · paying off · payoff (sustantivo)
errors_es: Entenderlo solo como 'liquidar una deuda'. Con una persona como objeto suele ser sobornar.

ex.en: Someone [paid off] the witness before the trial.
ex.es: Alguien sobornó al testigo antes del juicio.

ex.en: He thinks he can [pay everyone off] and walk away.
ex.es: Cree que puede comprar a todos y salirse con la suya.

ex.en: The cop was [paid off] to look the other way.
ex.es: Le pagaron al policía para que se hiciera de la vista gorda.

sense: gradually become smaller, weaker or less until it ends
es: irse apagando; desvanecerse poco a poco
def: to slowly become less and less until it stops completely
note: Sujetos típicos: a conversation, a relationship, a road, interest, a storm. No es nombre propio: peter va en minúscula.
forms: peter out · petered out · petering out
errors_es: Usar 'finish slowly'. Para algo que se apaga solo, sin final claro: peter out.

ex.en: The conversation [petered out] after a few minutes.
ex.es: La plática se fue apagando después de unos minutos.

ex.en: Our friendship kind of [petered out] after college.
ex.es: Nuestra amistad como que se fue desvaneciendo después de la universidad.

ex.en: The trail [peters out] near the lake, so bring a map.
ex.es: El sendero se va perdiendo cerca del lago, así que lleva un mapa.

sense: (phone it in) do something with very little effort or interest
es: hacer algo con desgano; cumplir por cumplir
def: to do your job or a performance with the minimum effort, as if you weren't really there
note: Casi siempre: phone it in. Crítica común a actores o trabajadores. Otro sentido: llamar a un programa o reportarse por teléfono.
forms: phone in · phoned in · phoning in · phoned-in (adjetivo)
errors_es: Entenderlo literal como 'llamar por teléfono'. 'He's phoning it in' = lo hace sin ganas.

ex.en: The lead actor was totally [phoning it in] this season.
ex.es: El actor principal de plano actuó sin ganas esta temporada.

ex.en: You can't [phone it in] when the client is watching.
ex.es: No puedes hacerlo con desgano cuando el cliente está viendo.

ex.en: Honestly, I [phoned in] that last essay.
ex.es: La verdad, ese último ensayo lo hice por cumplir.

sense: criticize something in great detail, finding every weakness
def: to look closely at an idea or argument and point out all its problems
note: Separable: pick it apart. Común en juicios: the lawyer picked his story apart.
forms: pick apart · picked apart · picking apart
errors_es: Decir 'criticize in pieces'. Para un análisis crítico implacable: pick it apart.

ex.en: The defense lawyer [picked apart] every detail of his story.
ex.es: El abogado defensor despedazó cada detalle de su versión.

ex.en: Please don't [pick apart] my plan before I finish explaining.
ex.es: Por favor no despedaces mi plan antes de que termine de explicarlo.

ex.en: Online, people [pick apart] every single episode.
ex.es: En internet la gente critica a detalle cada episodio.

sense: join others in criticizing or attacking someone
es: sumarse a las críticas; cargarle la mano a
def: to criticize or attack someone together with many other people, or to add a lot of something
note: Muy de redes: everyone piled on him. Sustantivo: pile-on. Transitivo: pile on the pressure / the guilt.
forms: pile on · piled on · piling on · pile-on (sustantivo)
errors_es: Decir 'everyone criticized him together'. Natural: everyone piled on (him).

ex.en: After his post, the whole internet [piled on].
ex.es: Después de su publicación, todo internet se le fue encima.

ex.en: Don't [pile on] the guilt, I already feel terrible.
ex.es: No me cargues la culpa, ya me siento fatal.

ex.en: His coworkers [piled on] once the boss started yelling.
ex.es: Sus compañeros se le fueron encima en cuanto el jefe empezó a gritar.

sense: blame someone for something, often unfairly
es: echarle la culpa a; colgarle (un delito) a
def: to make people believe someone did something bad, often when they didn't
note: Estructura: pin something on someone. Clásico de series: You're not pinning this on me!
forms: pin on · pinned on · pinning on
errors_es: Decir 'put the blame in me'. Natural: blame me / pin it on me.

ex.en: You can't [pin this on] me, I wasn't even there!
ex.es: ¡No me puedes echar la culpa, ni siquiera estaba ahí!

ex.en: They [pinned the robbery on] the new guy.
ex.es: Le colgaron el robo al nuevo.

ex.en: He's trying to [pin it on] his brother.
ex.es: Le quiere echar la culpa a su hermano.

sense: use someone's fears or weaknesses to get what you want
def: to use someone's feelings, fears or weak points to your advantage
note: Inseparable: play on people's fears. Otro sentido: a play on words = juego de palabras.
forms: play on · played on · playing on
errors_es: Usar 'play with' (jugar con). Para explotar miedos o culpas: play on.

ex.en: Scammers [play on] people's fear of losing money.
ex.es: Los estafadores se aprovechan del miedo de la gente a perder dinero.

ex.en: She knows how to [play on] my guilt.
ex.es: Sabe muy bien cómo usar mi culpa en mi contra.

ex.en: The ad [plays on] parents' worries about safety.
ex.es: El anuncio explota la preocupación de los papás por la seguridad.

sense: work through a large amount of something slowly and with effort
es: echarse; avanzar a fuerzas (con mucho trabajo)
def: to read, eat or do a big amount of something, slowly and with effort
note: Ortografía de EE. UU. y Canadá: plow (británico: plough). Común: plow through emails / paperwork / a book.
forms: plow through · plowed through · plowing through
errors_es: Traducirlo como 'arar'. Con trabajo o lectura es avanzar a fuerzas por mucho material.

ex.en: I [plowed through] two hundred emails this morning.
ex.es: Me eché doscientos correos esta mañana.

ex.en: She's [plowing through] the paperwork for the mortgage.
ex.es: Está avanzando a fuerzas con el papeleo de la hipoteca.

ex.en: The truck [plowed through] the snowbank and kept going.
ex.es: La camioneta atravesó el montón de nieve y siguió.

sense: study or read something very carefully for a long time
def: to look at or read something with great attention, usually for a long time
note: Inseparable: pore over the files. No confundir con pour (verter): suenan casi igual.
forms: pore over · pored over · poring over
errors_es: Escribir 'pour over'. Se dice igual, pero 'pore over' es estudiar a fondo.

ex.en: Detectives [pored over] the phone records all night.
ex.es: Los detectives se clavaron toda la noche en los registros telefónicos.

ex.en: I've been [poring over] these contracts since Monday.
ex.es: Llevo desde el lunes revisando a fondo estos contratos.

ex.en: She [pores over] recipes before every dinner party.
ex.es: Se clava en las recetas antes de cada cena con invitados.

sense: tell someone all your feelings or problems
es: desahogarse; contar todo (lo que se siente)
def: to express strong feelings or tell all your problems to someone
note: Frase fija: pour your heart out (to someone). También literal: servir una bebida.
forms: pour out · poured out · pouring out
errors_es: Decir 'empty my heart'. Natural: pour my heart out (to you).

ex.en: I [poured my heart out] and he just checked his phone.
ex.es: Le abrí mi corazón y él nada más vio su celular.

ex.en: She [poured out] all her frustrations to the therapist.
ex.es: Le contó todas sus frustraciones a la terapeuta.

ex.en: He finally [poured out] the whole story over coffee.
ex.es: Por fin soltó toda la historia tomando un café.

sense: support something or someone that would otherwise fail
es: sostener; apuntalar (a una empresa, a alguien)
def: to help something or someone keep going, often with money, when it would fail alone
note: Separable: prop it up. Literal: sostener algo para que no se caiga (prop up the door, prop yourself up on a pillow).
forms: prop up · propped up · propping up
errors_es: Usar 'sustain' para dinero de rescate. Para mantener algo a flote: prop up.

ex.en: The government spent billions [propping up] the banks.
ex.es: El gobierno gastó miles de millones en apuntalar a los bancos.

ex.en: His parents are still [propping up] his failing business.
ex.es: Sus papás todavía le sostienen el negocio que va mal.

ex.en: [Prop up] his head with a pillow so he can breathe.
ex.es: Levántale la cabeza con una almohada para que pueda respirar.

sense: make an opponent nervous so they perform worse
def: to make someone feel nervous or less confident, especially before a game or test
note: Separable: psych him out. 'Psych' se pronuncia /saɪk/ (la p es muda). Contrario de psych up (mentalizar).
forms: psych out · psyched out · psyching out
errors_es: Pronunciar la 'p'. Se dice /saɪk/. Tampoco es 'psicoanalizar'.

ex.en: He stares at you just to [psych you out].
ex.es: Te clava la mirada nada más para ponerte nervioso.

ex.en: Don't let the other team [psych you out].
ex.es: No dejes que el otro equipo te intimide.

ex.en: I totally got [psyched out] before my driving test.
ex.es: Me puse súper nervioso antes de mi examen de manejo.

sense: explain an idea so that people understand it clearly
def: to communicate an idea or opinion clearly so others understand it
note: Separable: put it across. Muy usado con well/clearly. Casi sinónimo de get across.
forms: put across · put across · putting across
errors_es: Decir 'transmit my idea'. 'Transmit' suena técnico; lo natural es get/put my point across.

ex.en: She [puts across] complex ideas in really simple words.
ex.es: Transmite ideas complejas con palabras muy sencillas.

ex.en: I didn't [put my point across] very well in that meeting.
ex.es: No supe hacer entender mi punto en esa junta.

ex.en: The ad [puts across] the message in ten seconds.
ex.es: El anuncio transmite el mensaje en diez segundos.

sense: cause someone trouble or extra work; (be put out) feel annoyed
es: causar molestia a; (be put out) molestarse
def: to give someone extra work or trouble, or (in the passive) to feel a little offended
note: Cortesía: I don't want to put you out. Pasiva: she seemed a bit put out = se notaba algo molesta.
forms: put out · put out · putting out · be put out
errors_es: Decir 'I don't want to molest you'. 'Molest' es abuso sexual; di 'I don't want to put you out'.

ex.en: Are you sure? I really don't want to [put you out].
ex.es: ¿Seguro? De verdad no quiero causarte molestias.

ex.en: She seemed a little [put out] that we didn't invite her.
ex.es: Se le notó un poco molesta de que no la invitáramos.

ex.en: It won't [put me out] at all, I'm driving that way.
ex.es: No es ninguna molestia, voy para allá de todas formas.

sense: send someone to prison or a mental hospital
def: to send someone to prison for a long time
note: Separable: put him away. Muy de series policiacas y judiciales: put him away for life. Otro sentido informal: comer mucho.
forms: put away · put away · putting away
errors_es: Entenderlo solo como 'guardar'. En contexto judicial es mandar a alguien a la cárcel.

ex.en: This evidence could [put him away] for twenty years.
ex.es: Esta evidencia podría meterlo a la cárcel veinte años.

ex.en: She's the lawyer who [put away] half the gang.
ex.es: Es la abogada que encerró a la mitad de la banda.

ex.en: If you testify, we can [put this guy away] for good.
ex.es: Si declaras, podemos encerrar a este tipo para siempre.

sense: tease someone by telling them something untrue as a joke
def: to try to make someone believe something false, as a joke
note: Casi siempre en progresivo y separado: You're putting me on! = ¡Me estás vacilando! EE. UU.
forms: put on · put on · putting on
errors_es: No reconocerlo y pensar en ropa. 'Are you putting me on?' = ¿me estás tomando el pelo?

ex.en: You won the lottery? You're [putting me on]!
ex.es: ¿Te sacaste la lotería? ¡Me estás vacilando!

ex.en: Relax, I was just [putting you on].
ex.es: Tranquilo, nada más te estaba tomando el pelo.

ex.en: I couldn't tell if he was [putting me on] or serious.
ex.es: No sabía si me estaba vacilando o hablaba en serio.

sense: show a certain amount of resistance or effort (put up a fight)
def: to fight, argue or resist in a certain way when something is done to you
note: Colocaciones fijas: put up a fight / resistance / a struggle / a good show. No se separa en este uso.
forms: put up · put up · putting up
errors_es: Decir 'make resistance'. Lo natural es put up a fight / put up resistance.

ex.en: The victim [put up] a fight, so look for scratches.
ex.es: La víctima opuso resistencia, así que busquen rasguños.

ex.en: Our team [put up] a good fight but lost in overtime.
ex.es: Nuestro equipo dio buena pelea, pero perdió en tiempo extra.

ex.en: I thought he'd [put up] more resistance to the idea.
ex.es: Pensé que se iba a oponer más a la idea.

sense: work out what happened by joining separate bits of information
def: to understand a story or event by putting many small facts together
note: Separable: piece it together. Típico de detectives y de la mañana después de una fiesta.
forms: piece together · pieced together · piecing together
errors_es: Decir 'reconstruct the facts' de forma rígida. Natural: piece together what happened.

ex.en: Police are still [piecing together] what happened that night.
ex.es: La policía todavía está reconstruyendo lo que pasó esa noche.

ex.en: I'm trying to [piece together] last night from these photos.
ex.es: Estoy tratando de reconstruir lo de anoche con estas fotos.

ex.en: She [pieced together] the truth from his texts.
ex.es: Armó la verdad a partir de sus mensajes.

sense: give a punishment or harsh treatment to someone
def: to give someone a punishment or unfair treatment
note: Formal, de noticias y juicios. Casi solo con punishment, justice, sentences. Rara vez se separa.
forms: mete out · meted out · meting out
errors_es: Pronunciarlo 'meté'. Se dice /mit/, como 'meet'.

ex.en: The judge [meted out] the toughest sentence possible.
ex.es: El juez impuso la sentencia más dura posible.

ex.en: Coaches shouldn't [mete out] punishment in front of the team.
ex.es: Los entrenadores no deberían castigar frente a todo el equipo.

ex.en: He believed he was [meting out] justice on his own.
ex.es: Creía que estaba haciendo justicia por su propia mano.

sense: hide a problem instead of dealing with it
def: to hide a problem or disagreement so it seems fine, without fixing it
note: Frase fija: paper over the cracks. Viene de tapar grietas de la pared con papel tapiz.
forms: paper over · papered over · papering over
errors_es: Usar 'cover with paper' literal. Figurado: paper over the problems = tapar el sol con un dedo.

ex.en: A bonus won't [paper over] the real problems on this team.
ex.es: Un bono no va a tapar los problemas de fondo de este equipo.

ex.en: They [papered over] their differences for the wedding.
ex.es: Disimularon sus diferencias por la boda.

ex.en: Stop [papering over] the cracks and talk to me.
ex.es: Ya deja de tapar el sol con un dedo y habla conmigo.

sense: reduce something to the most basic or necessary parts
def: to make something smaller or simpler by removing parts that are not needed
note: Separable: pare it down. Adjetivo: pared-down (minimalista). Común con list, budget, team, design.
forms: pare down · pared down · paring down · pared-down
errors_es: Confundir con 'pair' o 'pear' (suenan igual). Pare = recortar.

ex.en: We need to [pare down] this list to five candidates.
ex.es: Tenemos que recortar esta lista a cinco candidatos.

ex.en: She [pared down] her closet to thirty pieces.
ex.es: Redujo su clóset a treinta prendas.

ex.en: The app feels faster since they [pared down] the menu.
ex.es: La app se siente más rápida desde que simplificaron el menú.

sense: find the answer to something confusing by thinking hard
def: to understand something difficult or confusing after thinking about it carefully
note: Separable: puzzle it out. Más común en el habla: figure out. Suena algo literario.
forms: puzzle out · puzzled out · puzzling out
errors_es: Usar 'puzzle' solo como rompecabezas. Como verbo con out es descifrar.

ex.en: It took me an hour to [puzzle out] his handwriting.
ex.es: Me tomó una hora descifrar su letra.

ex.en: Scientists are still [puzzling out] how the virus spreads.
ex.es: Los científicos todavía están desentrañando cómo se propaga el virus.

ex.en: Let the kids [puzzle it out] on their own.
ex.es: Deja que los niños lo descifren solos.

sense: avoid saying or doing something directly because you are cautious
es: andarse con rodeos; no ir al grano
def: to act too carefully and avoid a clear decision or a direct answer
note: Informal, no vulgar (viene de los pasos de gato). Común: Stop pussyfooting around and tell me.
forms: pussyfoot around · pussyfooted around · pussyfooting around
errors_es: Pensar que es grosería. No lo es; significa andarse con rodeos.

ex.en: Stop [pussyfooting around] and tell me what's wrong.
ex.es: Ya deja de andarte con rodeos y dime qué pasa.

ex.en: The board [pussyfooted around] the layoffs for months.
ex.es: La junta le dio vueltas a los despidos durante meses.

ex.en: I'm not going to [pussyfoot around]: you're fired.
ex.es: No me voy a andar con rodeos: estás despedido.

sense: force your way into a situation or business that others control
es: meterse a la fuerza (en algo ajeno)
def: to use power or pressure to get involved in something that belongs to others
note: Casi siempre con on: muscle in on our territory / deal. Típico de mafias y negocios agresivos.
forms: muscle in · muscled in · muscling in
errors_es: Pensar en 'músculo' literal. Significa meterse a la fuerza en un negocio o territorio ajeno.

ex.en: A rival gang is trying to [muscle in] on our turf.
ex.es: Una banda rival se quiere meter a la fuerza en nuestro territorio.

ex.en: Big chains [muscled in] and the local shops closed.
ex.es: Las grandes cadenas llegaron a la fuerza y cerraron las tiendas locales.

ex.en: He always [muscles in] on other people's projects.
ex.es: Siempre se mete a la fuerza en los proyectos de otros.

sense: miss and want someone or something very much, often sadly
def: to want someone or something very much, especially someone or something you can't have
note: Tono algo literario o irónico. Inseparable: pine for someone. Pine = también pino.
forms: pine for · pined for · pining for
errors_es: Usar 'miss' cuando hay anhelo romántico intenso. 'Pine for' añade tristeza y deseo.

ex.en: He spent the whole summer [pining for] his ex.
ex.es: Se pasó todo el verano suspirando por su ex.

ex.en: I'm not [pining for] the old job, trust me.
ex.es: No extraño para nada el trabajo anterior, créeme.

ex.en: She still [pines for] the mountains back home.
ex.es: Todavía añora las montañas de su tierra.

sense: divide something into parts and give them to different people
def: to split something into portions and share them among people
note: Separable: parcel it out. Común con tasks, land, money, work.
forms: parcel out · parceled out · parceling out (Canadá: parcelled)
errors_es: Pensar en paquetería. Aquí 'parcel out' es repartir en porciones.

ex.en: Let's [parcel out] the tasks so nobody gets overloaded.
ex.es: Repartamos las tareas para que nadie quede saturado.

ex.en: The land was [parceled out] among the five siblings.
ex.es: El terreno se repartió entre los cinco hermanos.

ex.en: She [parcels out] the candy so it lasts all week.
ex.es: Reparte los dulces para que le duren toda la semana.
